name: The University of Edinburgh

settingEvidence.evidence: a city with an irresistible blend of history, natural beauty and modern city life.

fees.text: £10,050 for the 2027/28 academic year for students from England, Wales and Northern Ireland (Edinburgh's 'Rest of UK' fee rate), for students starting or continuing in 2027. It was £9,790 for 2026/27 starters. Edinburgh says fees rise each year in line with the UK Government fee cap.

source.evidence: If you are starting or continuing your studies in 2027, the fee for the 2027-28 academic year will be £10,050.

livingCosts.text: Edinburgh estimates about £1,546 a month for a single undergraduate in 2026/27: £13,914 for a 39-week academic year, or £18,552 for a full year. University halls average about £925 a month rent self-catered (range £414-£1,348) and £1,169 a month catered with two meals a day (range £842-£1,518), with utilities included, on 39-week leases.

source.evidence: we estimate that it will cost an average of £1,546 each month to live in Edinburgh as a single undergraduate student. This equates to £13,914 for a 39-week academic year and £18,552 for a full year.

openDays.text: Next undergraduate Open Day: Saturday 24 October 2026 (booking required). Open Days in 2027 will be in June and autumn 2027; dates will be published by January 2027.

source.evidence: Our next undergraduate Open Day will take place at the University on Saturday 24 October.

contextual.summary: Edinburgh gives widening access offers: a 'Plus Flag' (normally an offer at the lower minimum entry requirements) or a 'Flag' (standard requirements, but you are prioritised where competition for places is high), based on your postcode, school, care/refugee/estranged/carer status and access programmes.
contextual.typicalReduction: Plus Flag applicants will normally be made an offer at the programme's minimum entry requirement (ABB for most of the Economics degrees recorded here, compared with a standard range of A*A*A* to A*AA); an offer is not guaranteed.

criteria.detail: Plus Flag: your home postcode is in the lowest Acorn quintile ('Acorn 6') and you attend a state school in England, Wales or Northern Ireland. (Flag, which keeps the standard offer but prioritises you: the second lowest Acorn quintile, 'Acorn 5', and a state school in England, Wales or Northern Ireland.)

Plus Flag: your home postcode is in the lowest POLAR quintile ('POLAR1') and you attend a state school in England, Wales or Northern Ireland. (Flag: the second lowest POLAR quintile, 'POLAR2', and a state school in England, Wales or Northern Ireland.)
Scotland only: your home postcode is in the lowest quintile of the Scottish Index of Multiple Deprivation ('SIMD20').

Scotland only: you attend one of Edinburgh's identified Scottish target schools (chosen for low progression to higher education, high free school meal entitlement and many SIMD20 postcodes) or a LEAPS Group 1 or Group 1 Plus school.
You are a refugee or an asylum seeker.
You are estranged from your parents or guardians and are under 25 at the start of your degree.
You are a carer and have completed one or more of Edinburgh's recognised bridging programmes.
You are undertaking a Scottish Wider Access Programme (SWAP) course or Edinburgh's own Access Programme (routes for college students and adult learners).

contextual.rulesText: You are eligible for a Plus Flag if you are permanently resident in the UK and fulfil one or more of the Plus Flag criteria. With a Plus Flag you will normally be made an offer at the minimum entry requirement, as long as you are predicted to meet it and have the required subjects; this is not guaranteed. A Flag (for example Acorn 5 or POLAR2 plus a state school in England, Wales or Northern Ireland) keeps the standard entry requirements but prioritises you for places on programmes where competition is high. Acorn and POLAR data are updated each May, so use Edinburgh's checker tool to see whether you qualify.

notes: Scottish university: the degrees recorded are 4-year MA (Hons) degrees. The A level offers are for students from the rest of the UK.

Edinburgh publishes the range of grades most applicants needed to receive an offer in recent years (for example A*A*A* to A*AA for Economics). The top of the range is recorded as the typical offer and the bottom as the low end.

Widening access: applicants assigned a Plus Flag are normally made an offer at the minimum entry requirement (ABB for most courses recorded here; A*BB including A* in Mathematics for Economics and Mathematics). This is recorded in each course's alternative offers.

Edinburgh is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry (https://uat-wp.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/01172717/Course_List_2027_Entry_Final.pdf) and no course page names an admissions test.

Psychology and Economics MA (Hons) (CZ81) says it is closed to new applications for 2027, so it was not recorded. Other Economics-related joint degrees not recorded because of the course limit: Economics and Statistics (LG13), Philosophy and Economics (VL51), Social Policy and Economics (LL41), Business with Strategic Economics (N1L1), Accounting and Finance (NN43) and Finance and Business (NN13).
Edinburgh says it guarantees an offer of University accommodation to eligible new single undergraduates from outside Edinburgh (see the accommodation page for the full criteria).

Edinburgh's own access projects for school pupils (Reach Edinburgh, ACES, YourEd, LEAPS and SHEP) are for pupils in Scottish schools or for law, medicine, veterinary medicine and art subjects, so no Edinburgh-run Year 12 programme for students in England was recorded.
The Open Day page gives 'Saturday 24 October' without a year; 24 October 2026 is a Saturday.
